newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus-based agency suspends Pakistan bank ratings.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus-based agency suspends Pakistan bank ratings.

text.p: Cyprus-based Capital Intelligence on Tuesday suspended the ratings of all rated institutions in Pakistan in view of the bleak outlook for the economy and uncertainty as to how the banking sector will be affected.
The specialist bank rating agency said that institutions affected by the latest action are the National Bank of Pakistan, Muslim Commercial Bank, Allied Bank and Askari Commercial Bank.
The agency suspended ratings of Habib Bank and United Bank in December 1996.

The five large banks, which account for almost 60 percent of total assets in the banking sector, suffer from large incidences of non-performing loans, under-capitalisation, overstaffing and high expenses.
Given the pivotal role these banks play on the economy, their vulnerability would be exposed if the current situation were to deteriorate, Capital Intelligence said.
While the private sector banks are in relatively good shape, any deterioration in the economy or public banking sector in general would also have an adverse impact on these smaller institutions.
Capital Intelligence said it would contuinue to monitor developments closely and ratings will be re-assigned as soon as prospects for the economy improve.
